text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak Constitutional Court on Wednesday ruled that the constitution can be changed by a referendum.
- The official campaign related to the forthcoming referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections ended on Wednesday. The two plebiscites will be held on Friday and Saturday.

- President Michal Kovac said the Constitutional Court's ruling confirmed that the two referendums will be held together as originally announced by the president and that the interior ministry now must complete distribution of ballots with four questions - three related to voting on NATO membership and one on direct election of the president.
- Shareholders of largest Slovak steel producer VSZ a.s. on Wednesday approved a net dividend of 40 crowns per a share from the 1996 after-tax profit of 1.35 billion crowns.
- VSZ plans to increase its net profit by some 6.8 percent year-on-year in 1997 to total 1.44 billion crowns.

- Slovak money market dealers said they expected interbank rates to stay at current high levels or even slightly increase in the near future, since the National Bank of Slovakia seems to be deliberately keeping the market short of liquidity.

- Slovak Railways will inaugurate on June 3 a new direct cargo route between Slovakia and the Dutch port of Rotterdam. The railway connection will start in the Slovak capital Bratislava but the route will be extended to the eastern Slovak cargo terminal Cierna Nad Tisou from July 6.

- Slovakia's revenues from tourism rose by 8.5 percent year-on-year in 1996 and totalled $672.8 million. The overall number of tourists visiting Slovakia last year increased by 48,300, or 5.3 percent, and totalled 951,300 people.
SME - Interior Minister Gustav Krajci said he had ordered the printing of new referendum ballots with only the three questions on NATO membership.
- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) has called for citizens to ignore ballots with only three referendum questions saying the minister's move was illegal.
- President Kovac has rejected a request by Interior Minister Krajci to postpone the referendum to a later date. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
